why: The supplier worked late every night so the brochures would be ready on time. The verb that goes with the deadline is meet.
印刷廠每晚加班，是為了讓手冊準時完成。和 the deadline 搭配的動詞是 meet。
usage: match means to go well with something, or to be equal to it. The new curtains match the carpet.
match 是「和…相配」或「與…相等」。例：The new curtains match the carpet.
catch a bus, a train or a flight; also to notice something. She ran to catch the 8:15 train.
catch 搭 bus、train、flight，也有「注意到」的意思。例：She ran to catch the 8:15 train.
suit someone means to be right or convenient for them. Does Thursday at ten suit you?
suit 某人是「適合、方便某人」。例：Does Thursday at ten suit you?

gloss.ex: We booked a booth at the trade show.
The brochure lists all our services.
Our supplier delivers every Monday.

why: The policy starts to apply on July 1. The fixed phrase for this is take effect, and the sentence has no into.
規定從 7 月 1 日起適用。固定說法是 take effect，而這句裡沒有 into。
usage: come into effect means the same, but it needs into. The new law comes into effect next month.
come into effect 意思相同，但一定要有 into。例：The new law comes into effect next month.
go into effect also means to start applying. The ban goes into effect on Monday.
go into effect 也是「開始生效」。例：The ban goes into effect on Monday.
make goes with a decision, an effort, a profit. We made a decision before lunch.
make 搭 a decision、an effort、a profit。例：We made a decision before lunch.

gloss.ex: Please read the revised contract.
The policy covers all full-time staff.
We booked the conference room for Friday.

why: The manager needs new printer cartridges, so she will order them. The fixed phrase is place an order for, and the sentence continues with for new printer cartridges.
經理需要新的墨水匣，所以要訂購。固定說法是 place an order for，句子接著就是 for new printer cartridges。
usage: set a goal, a date or a price: you decide it. We set a date for the launch.
set 搭 goal、date、price，是「訂定」。例：We set a date for the launch.
lay something down means to put it flat; lay off means to dismiss workers. Please lay the documents on my desk.
lay 是「把東西平放」；lay off 是「裁員」。例：Please lay the documents on my desk.
position something means to put it in a particular place. The designer positioned the logo at the top.
position 是「把東西放在特定位置」。例：The designer positioned the logo at the top.

gloss.ex: The printer needs a new cartridge.

gloss.w: before the end of the day
gloss.hw: before the end of the day
gloss.ex: Please send the files before the end of the day.

point: keep a close eye on：密切注意。
why: The accountant wants the team to watch cash flow carefully during the slow summer months. The fixed phrase is keep a close eye on.
會計師要團隊在生意清淡的夏季密切注意 cash flow。固定說法是 keep a close eye on。
usage: hold a meeting, an event or a position. We hold a staff meeting every Monday.
hold 搭 meeting、event、position。例：We hold a staff meeting every Monday.
take a look at something, or take a break. Can you take a look at this contract?
take 搭 a look at、a break。例：Can you take a look at this contract?
set eyes on means to see, usually for the first time. She loved the house the moment she set eyes on it.
set eyes on 是「看見」，通常指第一次看到。例：She loved the house the moment she set eyes on it.

gloss.ex: Our accountant checks the books monthly.
The consultant recommends a smaller budget.
Cash flow is tight this quarter.

point: strike a balance between…：在…之間取得平衡。
why: The new schedule balances two things: client visits and time in the office. The fixed phrase is strike a balance between, so the verb is strike.
新班表要平衡兩件事：client visits 和 time in the office。固定說法是 strike a balance between，所以動詞是 strike。
usage: pull means to draw something toward you. He pulled the door open.
pull 是「拉」。例：He pulled the door open.
run a business, a team or a test. She runs a small design studio.
run 搭 business、team、test，是「經營、執行」。例：She runs a small design studio.
lift something up, or lift a ban or a restriction. The city lifted the parking ban.
lift 是「舉起」，或「解除」禁令、限制。例：The city lifted the parking ban.

gloss.ex: We offer flexible working hours.
We aim to reply within one business day.
Client visits take up most of my week.

why: Most of the shareholders voted yes at the meeting, a very large majority. The fixed phrase for that is an overwhelming majority.
會議上絕大多數股東投贊成票。形容這種多數的固定說法是 an overwhelming majority。
usage: overflowing means so full that things spill out. The overflowing bin needs to be emptied.
overflowing 是「滿到溢出來」。例：The overflowing bin needs to be emptied.
overpowering describes a smell, feeling or force that is too strong. The overpowering smell of paint filled the room.
overpowering 形容氣味、感覺或力量太強烈。例：The overpowering smell of paint filled the room.
overriding means more important than anything else. Safety is our overriding concern.
overriding 是「比什麼都重要的」。例：Safety is our overriding concern.

gloss.ex: The bank opened a new branch downtown.
A majority of staff prefer the new schedule.
Shareholders will vote on the merger.

why: Although orders rose sharply, revenue still did not reach the target. The phrase for missing a goal is fall short of; the past form is fell.
雖然訂單大增，營收仍沒達到 the target。未達目標的說法是 fall short of，過去式是 fell。
usage: run short of something means to have too little of it left. We are running short of printer paper.
run short of 是「某物快不夠用」。例：We are running short of printer paper.
cut something short means to end it early. A fire alarm cut the meeting short.
cut … short 是「提前結束」。例：A fire alarm cut the meeting short.
draw attention, a conclusion or a picture. The new ad drew a lot of attention.
draw 搭 attention、conclusion、picture。例：The new ad drew a lot of attention.

gloss.ex: Prices rose sharply last month.
Revenue grew by five percent.
Sales were strong in the first quarter.

point: lodge a complaint：正式提出申訴。
why: Customers with a damaged delivery must make a formal complaint in writing. Lodge means to submit something officially, and it goes with a formal complaint.
貨品受損的顧客必須以書面正式提出申訴。lodge 是「正式提出」，和 a formal complaint 搭配。
usage: house means to provide a home or space for someone or something. The new building will house our legal team.
house 當動詞是「為…提供住處或空間」。例：The new building will house our legal team.
host an event or a party: to organize it for guests. The hotel will host the awards dinner.
host 搭 event、party，是「主辦」並招待賓客。例：The hotel will host the awards dinner.
board a plane, a train or a ship: to get on it. Passengers may board the train now.
board 是「登上」飛機、火車或船。例：Passengers may board the train now.

gloss.ex: Please confirm the offer in writing.
Attach the receipt to your claim form.
The packaging protects the glass.

point: bear in mind that…：記住、留意。
why: The writer asks guests to keep one fact in mind: the visitor parking garage will be closed on Saturday. The phrase is bear in mind that, and that introduces the fact.
作者要來賓記住一件事：訪客停車場星期六關閉。說法是 bear in mind that，that 後面接要記住的事。
usage: take something into account means to consider it. Please take the cost into account.
take … into account 是「把…納入考量」。例：Please take the cost into account.
put means to place something somewhere. Please put the boxes in the storage room.
put 是「把東西放在某處」。例：Please put the boxes in the storage room.
carry means to hold and move something, or to have it with you. Staff must carry their ID badges.
carry 是「攜帶、搬運」。例：Staff must carry their ID badges.

gloss.ex: The school holds an open house in May.
Over fifty guests are attending the dinner.
Please park in the lot behind the office.

point: commission: pay as a share of sales.
commission 佣金：按成交金額抽成。
why: Reps get 4 percent on every contract they sign, on top of their base salary. Pay that is a share of each sale is a commission.
業務每簽一份合約抽 4%，另外還有底薪。按每筆成交抽成的錢是 commission。
usage: wage is pay for hours or days worked, often paid weekly. The hourly wage rose to $18.
wage 是按時數或天數計的工資。例：The hourly wage rose to $18.
pension is money paid regularly after someone retires. He receives a pension from his former employer.
pension 是退休後定期領的退休金。例：He receives a pension from his former employer.
allowance is a set amount given for a cost such as travel or housing. The company pays a monthly travel allowance.
allowance 是為交通、住房等費用給的固定津貼。例：The company pays a monthly travel allowance.

gloss.ex: Each sales representative covers one region.
Her base salary is paid monthly.
In addition to salary, staff get a bonus.

point: lend = give for a time; borrow = take for a time.
why: The IT department gives laptops to staff and wants them back within two weeks. The next clause calls staff borrowers, so the department lends the equipment.
資訊部把筆電交給員工，兩週內要收回。後句稱員工為 borrowers，所以資訊部是借出，用 lends。
usage: return means to give something back, or to come back. Please return the projector to the IT desk.
return 是「歸還」或「回來」。例：Please return the projector to the IT desk.
borrow means to take something from someone for a short time. May I borrow your charger?
borrow 是「向人借入」。例：May I borrow your charger?
donate means to give something for free, with nothing coming back. The firm donated old computers to a school.
donate 是「捐出」，不會收回。例：The firm donated old computers to a school.

gloss.ex: The team held an off-site workshop.
Borrowers must sign for each item.
The projector in room B is broken.

why: Guests who use room service or minibar create extra charges that they must pay. The verb for bringing a cost on yourself is incur.
使用 room service 或 minibar 的房客會產生額外費用，要自己付。「招致費用」的動詞是 incur。
usage: suffer a loss, an injury or a delay: something bad happens to you. The company suffered a heavy loss last year.
suffer 搭 loss、injury、delay，是「遭受」不好的事。例：The company suffered a heavy loss last year.
undergo a process, test or change. All new staff undergo a week of training.
undergo 搭 process、test、change，是「經歷」。例：All new staff undergo a week of training.
endure means to put up with something painful or difficult. Travelers endured a long delay at the airport.
endure 是「忍受」痛苦或困難。例：Travelers endured a long delay at the airport.

gloss.ex: We ordered room service for breakfast.
The minibar is stocked with drinks.
Please settle your bill at the front desk.
Checkout is at eleven in the morning.

why: The sentence names the whole, the new advisory committee, and puts its members, five managers, right after the verb. With no of, the verb is comprises.
句子先說整體 the new advisory committee，成員 five managers 緊接在動詞後。沒有 of，所以用 comprises。
usage: consist of means to be made up of; it needs of. The team consists of six engineers.
consist of 是「由…組成」，要有 of。例：The team consists of six engineers.
conform to means to follow a rule or standard. All products must conform to safety standards.
conform to 是「符合」規定或標準。例：All products must conform to safety standards.
constitute means to make up a whole, so the members are the subject. Women constitute half of our workforce.
constitute 是「構成」整體，主詞是成員。例：Women constitute half of our workforce.

gloss.ex: The advisory committee meets every quarter.
The marketing department is on the third floor.

point: Read the whole sentence: markedly = by a large amount.
看全句：markedly 是明顯地、大幅地。
why: Visits went up by 40 percent (jumping 40 percent) in the first week, a large rise, and stayed at that level for the rest of the year. So the adverb is markedly.
來客數跳升 40%，是大幅增加，而且之後維持在那個水準到年底。所以副詞是 markedly。
usage: slightly means by a small amount. Prices rose slightly in March.
slightly 是「稍微」。例：Prices rose slightly in March.
steadily means at an even pace over time. Sales have grown steadily since January.
steadily 是「穩定、逐步地」。例：Sales have grown steadily since January.
temporarily means for a short time only. The store is temporarily closed for cleaning.
temporarily 是「暫時地」。例：The store is temporarily closed for cleaning.

gloss.ex: The showroom displays our newest models.
The renovation took three months.
Orders jumped after the new ad ran.

why: The rent stays the same for another two years, so the lease gets longer in time. The verb for making a period longer is extend.
租金不變，租約再多兩年，也就是期限變長。讓期間變長的動詞是 extend。
usage: expand means to grow bigger in size, amount or reach. The firm plans to expand into Asia.
expand 是規模、數量或範圍變大。例：The firm plans to expand into Asia.
enlarge means to make something bigger, such as a photo or a room. We enlarged the photo for the poster.
enlarge 是把照片、空間等放大。例：We enlarged the photo for the poster.
stretch means to pull something longer, or to make it last. We must stretch the budget to cover repairs.
stretch 是「拉長」，或讓預算等撐久一點。例：We must stretch the budget to cover repairs.

gloss.ex: The landlord fixed the heating.
We signed a three-year lease.

point: abide by the rules：遵守規定。
why: The blank is followed by by the safety rules. Of the four words that mean to obey, only abide takes by: abide by.
空格後面是 by the safety rules。四個「遵守」的字裡，只有 abide 接 by：abide by。
usage: comply with a rule, request or law. All vendors must comply with the new regulations.
comply with 是「遵守」規則、要求或法律。例：All vendors must comply with the new regulations.
adhere to a rule, plan or schedule. Please adhere to the agreed timeline.
adhere to 是「遵守」規則、計畫或時程。例：Please adhere to the agreed timeline.
conform to a rule or standard. The packaging must conform to export standards.
conform to 是「符合」規則或標準。例：The packaging must conform to export standards.

gloss.ex: The subcontractor finished the wiring.
Notices are posted on the wall.
Visitors must wear a hard hat.

why: The plant stops production for two weeks, and normal operations will resume on September 1. A stop that ends and then restarts is suspend.
工廠停產兩週，9 月 1 日正常營運恢復。先停下來、之後再恢復的是 suspend。
usage: terminate means to end something for good, such as a contract. The company terminated the agreement.
terminate 是「終止」，例如合約。例：The company terminated the agreement.
abandon means to give something up completely. They abandoned the project after the budget was cut.
abandon 是「完全放棄」。例：They abandoned the project after the budget was cut.
conclude means to finish, or to reach a decision. The talks concluded on Friday.
conclude 是「結束」或「下結論」。例：The talks concluded on Friday.

gloss.ex: The packaging line runs two shifts.
The technician installed the new printer.
Work will resume on Monday.

why: The blank is followed directly by the thing that is dropped: the cancellation fee. Only waive takes a fee as its object; the hotel agrees not to charge it.
空格後直接接被免掉的東西：the cancellation fee。只有 waive 以費用當受詞；飯店同意不收這筆費用。
usage: exempt someone from a rule or charge. The law exempts small firms from this tax.
exempt 人 from 規定或費用。例：The law exempts small firms from this tax.
spare someone something unpleasant. The early flight spared us a long wait.
spare 人 + 麻煩事，是「讓人免去」。例：The early flight spared us a long wait.
relieve someone of a duty or burden; also to ease pain. The assistant relieved the manager of routine tasks.
relieve 人 of 責任或負擔；也有「緩解」之意。例：The assistant relieved the manager of routine tasks.

gloss.ex: A cancellation fee applies after Monday.
You may enter provided that you sign in.
We need written confirmation of the order.

why: The document came from the travel agent and lists flight times and the address of each hotel. A trip plan with times and places is an itinerary.
這份文件來自旅行社，列出航班時間和每間飯店的地址。列出時間與地點的旅程計畫就是 itinerary。
usage: inventory is the list or stock of goods a business holds. We count our inventory every December.
inventory 是公司持有的庫存或庫存清單。例：We count our inventory every December.
agenda is the list of topics for a meeting. The agenda has five items.
agenda 是會議的議程。例：The agenda has five items.
warranty is a written promise to repair or replace a product. The printer has a two-year warranty.
warranty 是產品的保固。例：The printer has a two-year warranty.

gloss.ex: Our travel agent booked the flights.
All fees are listed on the form.

why: The supplier sent the document for the 40 chairs, and it is payable within 30 days. A bill that asks you to pay is an invoice.
供應商寄來 40 張椅子的單據，要在 30 天內付款。要求你付款的單據是 invoice。
usage: receipt is proof that you have already paid. Keep the receipt in case you return the item.
receipt 是已付款的收據。例：Keep the receipt in case you return the item.
estimate is an approximate price given before work begins. The contractor gave us a written estimate.
estimate 是開工前給的概略報價。例：The contractor gave us a written estimate.
refund is money given back to a customer. She asked for a refund after the order arrived damaged.
refund 是退還給顧客的錢。例：She asked for a refund after the order arrived damaged.

gloss.ex: Our supplier delivers every Monday.
The fee is payable by check.

why: The launch is moved to next Thursday, a later date, because of the storm warning. Moving an event to a later time is postponed.
因為 the storm warning，發表會改到 next Thursday。把活動挪到之後舉行就是 postponed。
usage: abandon means to give something up completely. The firm abandoned the plan to open a new store.
abandon 是「完全放棄」。例：The firm abandoned the plan to open a new store.
expire means to reach the end of a valid period. My passport expires in May.
expire 是證件、合約等「到期」。例：My passport expires in May.
conclude means to finish, or to end a talk or deal. The meeting concluded at noon.
conclude 是「結束」會議或交易。例：The meeting concluded at noon.

gloss.ex: A storm warning is in effect tonight.
The product launch drew many reporters.

point: deduct A from B：從 B 扣除 A。
why: The uniform cost is taken from your first month's salary. The word from points to deducted: be deducted from.
制服費用從第一個月的薪水中扣。from 是線索，指向 deducted：be deducted from。
usage: reduce means to make something smaller or less. We reduced our energy use by ten percent.
reduce 是「減少」。例：We reduced our energy use by ten percent.
decline means to say no politely, or to become lower. She declined the invitation.
decline 是「婉拒」或「下降」。例：She declined the invitation.
devote time or effort to something. He devoted the morning to the budget.
devote 時間或心力 to 某事。例：He devoted the morning to the budget.

gloss.ex: The staff uniform includes a name badge.
Her salary is paid on the 25th.

why: Staff pay for fuel with their own cars, and the company pays them back at a fixed rate. Paying back money an employee spent is reimbursed.
員工開自己的車、先付油錢，公司再按固定費率還給他們。把員工代墊的錢還回去就是 reimbursed。
usage: reward means to give something for good work. The firm rewarded her for finding the error.
reward 是「獎勵」表現好。例：The firm rewarded her for finding the error.
recruit means to find and hire new people. We plan to recruit ten engineers.
recruit 是「招募」新人。例：We plan to recruit ten engineers.
reserve means to book something in advance, or to keep it for someone. I reserved a table for six.
reserve 是「預訂」或「保留」。例：I reserved a table for six.

gloss.ex: Fuel costs rose again this year.
We charge a fixed rate per hour.

point: absorb the cost：自行吸收費用。
why: The delay was its own error, so the shipping company takes the extra cost on itself instead of charging the customer. That is absorb.
延誤是物流公司自己的錯，所以多出來的費用由它自己承擔，不向客戶收。這就是 absorb。
usage: adopt means to start using a plan, policy or method. The firm adopted a new return policy.
adopt 是「採用」計畫、政策或方法。例：The firm adopted a new return policy.
attach a file or document to an email or a form. Please attach your resume to the form.
attach 是把檔案或文件「附上」。例：Please attach your resume to the form.
acquire means to get a company, a skill or an asset. The firm acquired a smaller rival.
acquire 是「取得」公司、技能或資產。例：The firm acquired a smaller rival.

gloss.ex: The shipping company delivers overnight.
The delay was caused by heavy snow.

point: deposit: part of the price paid first.
why: Pellham receives 15 percent of the purchase price when the agreement is signed, and the balance is due on delivery. A first part-payment is a deposit.
Pellham 在簽約時先收價款的 15%，餘款 the balance 交貨時付。先付的一部分款項是 deposit。
usage: dividend is a share of profit paid to shareholders. The company paid a quarterly dividend.
dividend 是公司發給股東的股利。例：The company paid a quarterly dividend.
rebate is part of the price returned to the buyer after payment. Buyers get a rebate on qualifying purchases.
rebate 是付款後退還給買方的一部分錢。例：Buyers get a rebate on qualifying purchases.
premium is the regular payment for insurance, or an extra charge. The insurance premium rises every year.
premium 是保費，或額外加價。例：The insurance premium rises every year.

gloss.ex: Under the terms of the lease, rent is monthly.
Please pay the balance by Friday.
Payment is due upon delivery.

point: reconcile A with B: check that two records match.
reconcile A with B：核對兩份帳使其相符。
why: The team compares bank statements with its internal ledger and looks into any discrepancies. Checking that two sets of records agree is reconcile.
會計組把 bank statements 和 internal ledger 比對，並查明任何不符之處。確認兩份紀錄一致就是 reconcile。
usage: consolidate means to combine several things into one. The firm consolidated three offices into one.
consolidate 是把幾個合併成一個。例：The firm consolidated three offices into one.
liquidate means to sell assets for cash, or to close a business and pay its debts. The owner liquidated the stock.
liquidate 是變賣資產，或清算結束公司。例：The owner liquidated the stock.
appraise means to judge the value of something. An expert will appraise the building.
appraise 是替東西估價。例：An expert will appraise the building.

gloss.ex: Enter each payment in the ledger.
We found a discrepancy in the totals.
The bank statement arrives monthly.

point: confidential 機密的；confident 有信心的。
why: Details of the merger must not leak before it is announced. Keep … strictly confidential means to keep every detail strictly secret.
合併案公布前，細節不能外洩。keep … strictly confidential 是把每個細節嚴格保密。
usage: confident means sure of yourself or of something. She is confident that the team will win.
confident 是「有信心的」。例：She is confident that the team will win.
confiding describes someone who shares private feelings with others. She spoke in a confiding tone.
confiding 形容人愛吐露心事、信任別人。例：She spoke in a confiding tone.
confided is the past of confide: to tell a secret to someone. She confided her plans to her manager.
confided 是 confide 的過去式，是向人透露祕密。例：She confided her plans to her manager.

gloss.ex: The merger created a larger firm.
Negotiations lasted three weeks.
Smoking is strictly forbidden here.

point: sensitive 敏感的；sensible 明智的。
why: The folder holds employee salaries and must be kept locked. Private information that should not be shared is sensitive.
這個資料夾裡有 employee salaries，必須上鎖。不該外流的私密資料就是 sensitive。
usage: sensible means wise and practical. Wearing a hard hat is a sensible precaution.
sensible 是「明智、合理的」。例：Wearing a hard hat is a sensible precaution.
sensory relates to the senses, such as sight and hearing. The exhibit offers a sensory experience.
sensory 是「感官的」，如視覺、聽覺。例：The exhibit offers a sensory experience.
senseless means without sense or purpose. The delay was a senseless waste of time.
senseless 是「沒有意義的」。例：The delay was a senseless waste of time.

gloss.ex: Please keep the cabinet locked.
Salaries are paid on the 25th.

why: Ms. Lin and Mr. Hale each present figures for their own region. Respective means each person's own, so it fits their respective regions.
林女士和 Hale 先生各自報告自己地區的數字。respective 是「各自的」，所以用 their respective regions。
usage: respectful means showing respect to others. The staff were respectful to all customers.
respectful 是「有禮貌、尊重人的」。例：The staff were respectful to all customers.
respectable means good enough to be approved of. The firm posted a respectable profit.
respectable 是「像樣、體面的」。例：The firm posted a respectable profit.
respected means admired by others. She is a respected scientist.
respected 是「受人尊敬的」。例：She is a respected scientist.

gloss.ex: The sales figures look strong this month.
Our largest region is the north.

point: industrious 勤奮的；industrial 工業的。
why: The interns always finish their tasks ahead of schedule, which shows they work hard. The word for hardworking people is industrious.
實習生總是提前完成工作，表示他們工作很努力。形容勤奮的人用 industrious。
usage: industrial means related to industry and factories. The company runs an industrial park.
industrial 是「工業的」。例：The company runs an industrial park.
industrialized describes a country with many factories and industries. Japan is an industrialized country.
industrialized 形容「已工業化的」國家。例：Japan is an industrialized country.
industrializing describes a country that is building up its industries. Many industrializing economies need new roads.
industrializing 形容「工業化中的」國家。例：Many industrializing economies need new roads.

gloss.ex: The manager praised her careful work.
Two interns joined the team in June.
The project finished ahead of schedule.

why: The manual was rewritten in plain language so that every new employee can understand it. Comprehensible to means easy for someone to understand.
手冊用淺白的語言重寫，好讓每位新員工看得懂。comprehensible to 是「對某人來說易懂」。
usage: comprehensive means complete and covering everything. The report gives a comprehensive review of sales.
comprehensive 是「全面的」。例：The report gives a comprehensive review of sales.
comprehending is the -ing form of comprehend, to understand. Comprehending the rules took her a week.
comprehending 是 comprehend（理解）的 -ing 形。例：Comprehending the rules took her a week.
comprehended is the past form of comprehend, to understand. She quickly comprehended the problem.
comprehended 是 comprehend 的過去式。例：She quickly comprehended the problem.

gloss.ex: The report was rewritten for clarity.
The contract uses plain language.

why: The store carries screws in every size one could think of, so builders rarely have to order parts. Every imaginable size means every size you can think of.
這家店的螺絲什麼尺寸都有，所以營造商很少要另外訂零件。every imaginable size 是所有想得到的尺寸。
usage: imaginative means full of new, creative ideas. The team came up with an imaginative design.
imaginative 是「有想像力、有創意的」。例：The team came up with an imaginative design.
imaginary means not real; it exists only in the mind. The map shows an imaginary line between the two regions.
imaginary 是「虛構的」，只存在於想像中。例：The map shows an imaginary line between the two regions.
imagine means to form a picture in your mind; imagining is its -ing form. I am imagining a bigger office.
imagining 是 imagine（想像）的 -ing 形。例：I am imagining a bigger office.

gloss.ex: The store stocks over a thousand items.
Please order two boxes of screws.
Our trains are rarely late.

why: Reviewers praise the staff for how they treat guests' needs, and requests are handled within minutes. Being attentive to needs means noticing and meeting them.
評論稱讚員工對 guests' needs 的態度，要求幾分鐘內就處理好。being attentive to 就是留意並滿足需求。
usage: attendant as an adjective means going along with something. The plan has attendant risks.
attendant 當形容詞是「伴隨而來的」。例：The plan has attendant risks.
attend means to be present at an event; attended is its past form. Over 200 people attended the seminar.
attended 是 attend（出席）的過去式。例：Over 200 people attended the seminar.
attend to means to deal with something; attending is the -ing form. She is attending to a customer.
attend to 是「處理、照料」；attending 是 -ing 形。例：She is attending to a customer.

gloss.ex: Reviewers liked the new menu.
The reception staff greet every guest.
Complaints are handled by the manager.

point: complimentary 免費贈送的；complementary 互補的。
why: Everyone who registers before May 1 receives a book, collected at the registration desk. A copy given as a free gift is complimentary.
五月一日前報名的人都會拿到一本書，到 the registration desk 領取。免費贈送的書是 complimentary。
usage: complementary means going well together or filling each other's gaps. Our skills are complementary.
complementary 是「互補的」。例：Our skills are complementary.
compliment means to praise someone; complimented is its past form. She complimented him on his speech.
complimented 是 compliment（稱讚）的過去式。例：She complimented him on his speech.
completed means finished or filled in. Please return the completed form.
completed 是「完成的、填好的」。例：Please return the completed form.

gloss.ex: The keynote speaker opened the conference.
Badges are at the registration desk.
Please pick up your badge at the desk.
